from_quote: By the eighth section of this article, Congress is to have power to lay and collect taxes, duties, imposts, and excises
rationale: The paragraph, an extract Centinel reprints from Luther Martin, quotes the opening words of the first clause of Article I, Section 8, which it names as "the eighth section of this article"; it also refers to the provision that duties, imposts and excises shall be uniform.
to_quote: have Power To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises

from_quote: by another part of the system no duties on exports were to be laid
rationale: The paragraph (an extract from Luther Martin) names "another part of the system" under which no duties on exports may be laid, which only this clause of Article I, Section 9 fits.

from_quote: by the fourth section of the first article, it is expressly provided, that the Congress shall have a power to make and alter all regulations concerning the time and manner of holding elections for senators
rationale: The paragraph (an extract from Luther Martin) names "the fourth section of the first article" and paraphrases its provision that Congress may make or alter regulations for the time and manner of holding elections for senators.
to_quote: Manner of holding Elections for Senators

from_quote: the patriotic essays of Brutus, Cincinnatus, Cato, etc., published at New York
rationale: The paragraph names the essays of Cato published at New York among the papers it says were withheld in the post and republished late in Philadelphia; it names the series, not a particular number.
